answer: One concrete defense is proof-of-personhood through decentralized in-person verification: communities gather at a local garden or library where verified members vouch for newcomers, and each gathering broadcasts a cryptographic beacon timestamp that anchors the ceremony to a public ledger. Like stalks of yarrow spreading from shared roots, reputations grow only through vetted human connections, so an attacker minting thousands of fake identities cannot cheaply fabricate the social history each account needs.
